accepted.evidence: Turner gives Gujarati kādav mud under kardama, beside Middle Indo-Aryan kaddama and Hindi kādaw. These Bhili-area forms preserve the diagnostic intervocalic v or its vocalic trace before a diminutive ḍ suffix. The kād- family comparison is secure at this level; expressive suffix and occasional aspiration are qualifications, and bare eastern kāda forms are excluded because karda competes.
